title: She proposed
hook: Khadijah, respected and independent, proposes marriage through a friend

segments.voice: Yesterday: Khadijah's caravan. Her goods went north to Syria, and Maysarah came home talking about the man who led it. Your line was: his honesty was the report.

A message leaves a merchant's house in Mecca, carried quietly by a friend. It comes from a woman of standing, with her own wealth and her own trade. It goes to a young man with no fortune at all. She has heard Maysarah's report about the man who led her caravan, weighed it, and made up her mind. The friend's question sounds casual: what's keeping him from marriage? It isn't casual at all. Today: she proposed.
screen: `A MESSAGE FROM A MERCHANT'S HOUSE.` → `TO A MAN WITH NO FORTUNE.` → `SHE PROPOSED.`

segments.voice: Khadijah wasn't marrying for money; she had her own goods on the road and men hired to trade them. What she was choosing was a person. In Ibn Ishaq's telling, she sends word to him with her reasons: the family tie between them, his good name among his people, his trustworthiness, his character, his truthfulness. Not his money; he had little. Another report, in Ibn Sa'd, says she first sent a friend, a woman named Nafisa, to ask him quietly what was keeping him from marriage. He said he had nothing to marry with. And Nafisa asked: and if that were taken care of, and you were invited by beauty, wealth, standing and a good match? So the go-between opened the door, and Khadijah walked through it. The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ told his uncles, the families met, and the marriage was made. The sources give different names for who spoke for her family; they agree on who asked first. Much later, the Qur'an describes what a marriage is meant to hold. In Pickthall's words: "He ordained between you love and mercy." And a hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari answers her choice from the other side. Years on, the angel Jibril comes to the Prophet and says: Khadijah is on her way to you with a dish of food. When she arrives, give her greetings of peace from her Lord, and from me. A woman who chose, and was greeted by name.
screen: `A MERCHANT WOMAN OF STANDING.` · `HER REASONS WERE HIS CHARACTER.` · `A FRIEND OPENS THE DOOR.` · `GREETINGS FROM HER LORD.` · then, large: `SHE CHOSE HIM.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind a woman who made a decision others wouldn't have made, and stood behind it: a grandmother, a boss, a teacher, a friend. Name, quietly and specifically, the reasons you trust her, the way Khadijah named hers. If you pray, ask good for her by name; if not, hold her in mind with gratitude.
She proposed. Khadijah, a merchant of standing, asked the Prophet to marry her, through a friend and with her own reasons, for the sake of his character. Today's word.
Your line: she chose him. Her reasons were about who he was. Day seven hundred seventeen, done.

howItsDone: Muslims remember Khadijah as Umm al-Mu'minin, a mother of the believers, and her proposal is often retold in talks on marriage and on the dignity of women in the Prophet's ﷺ life.

chat.meaning: The sources agree Khadijah asked first. Her reasons were kinship, his good name, trustworthiness, character and truthfulness, not money.

notes: Ages left out on purpose (the common figures of 25 and 40 are reports, and some early reports make her younger); year 1 day 83 already gave them as tradition.
Her list of reasons is paraphrased from Ibn Ishaq (Guillaume p. 82 area); confirm the items and that she said them to him directly.
Nafisa bint Munya as go-between and the 'nothing to marry with' exchange are from Ibn Sa'd; confirm wording of the paraphrase.
Who spoke for Khadijah's family varies (her father Khuwaylid in Ibn Ishaq, her uncle Amr ibn Asad in other reports); the script says only that the sources differ.
Pickthall 30:21 fragment quoted from memory ('and He ordained between you love and mercy'); confirm wording.
Sahih al-Bukhari 3820: confirm number; the hadith also gives glad tidings of a house in Paradise, omitted here.

Editor: rewrote the hook to drop an unsourced claim about how Meccan proposals usually ran; changed 'every reason is about the kind of man he was' (kinship is not character) to 'her reasons are about who he was'; 'a later report' to 'another report'.

Audit: Ibn Ishaq has Khadijah send her reasons to him by message ('she sent to him and said'), not say them 'to his face'; teach and word line corrected. 'She didn't need a husband to be secure' (an unsourced read of her inner state) changed to 'she wasn't marrying for money'.
